$what: Every place the standard must ask a human instead of deciding for them.
$why: The rule already existed in prose and did not hold. onboard.md said to mark inferred work
unconfirmed and put the interview in the backlog; a full adoption ran without doing it.
A point listed here is not advice - it is a declared call site, checked statically in CI
and asserted by replay against the fixture repos.
$point_id_contract: Every AskUserQuestion call lists the ids of the points it asks in metadata.source, space-separated - a field the person answering never sees, so the header can say Evidence rather than [adopt.evidence], which read as code to the first adopters and does not fit the header's twelve characters anyway. Without the id the replay layer cannot assert which points were reached, only how many questions were asked - and count is exactly the metric that let this defect hide. A bracketed [id] in the header is still read, for transcripts and adopted repositories from before 1.0.4.

answer_kinds.answer: The human decides now. -> provenance human.
answer_kinds.suggest: The agent proposes, the human verifies later. -> provenance provisional, plus a backlog row naming this point. Counts as human presence: it is attributable, timestamped, and produces a marked artifact.
answer_kinds.stub: Placeholder only, the agent must not guess. -> provenance absent, with a visible gap marker.
answer_kinds.defer: Not now, ask again at the next checkpoint. -> nothing is written.

provenance_states.pending: The run has not reached this point yet. A freshly scaffolded repo starts here, and it is not a resting place: once a path this point gates holds an artifact that did not ship as a template, something was written where the question belonged, and a row still pending is an adoption that stopped halfway.
provenance_states.human: Answered by a person; verifiable against the session transcript.
provenance_states.provisional: Agent-authored under an explicit 'suggest' choice; awaiting verification.
provenance_states.inferred: Agent concluded it from the repository and said so. Never valid where the answer is a preference rather than a fact.
provenance_states.absent: Deliberately left empty under a 'stub' choice.
provenance_states.unverified: Claimed human, no transcript to check it against. Counted separately, never folded into 'validated'.

points.asks: Which language do the written artifacts use - code and commits in English with docs and specs in yours, all of it in English, or all of it in yours?
points.recommended: code and commits in English, docs and specs in mine
points.why: AGENTS.md has carried a `Working language` slot from the beginning and nothing ever asked for it, so it gets filled with whatever the agent was already writing in - which is English, because the standard is written in English. That is a decision about the repository made by accident. The split leads because it is the one the standard's own template names, and because it is what most teams actually want: the toolchain speaks English, the people do not have to.
points.gates: AGENTS.md - the Working language line under Conventions

points.asks: This repository already names and arranges things its own way, and the standard names them differently. Move what you have into the standard's layout, keep yours and map the standard onto it, or decide case by case?
points.recommended: move ours into the standard's layout
points.gates: any rename or move of a path the repository already tracks
points.why: A repository's own naming is a decision someone already made. Overwriting it silently is the most destructive thing an adoption can do, because it looks like tidying.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: commit 24d36b8c moved docs/ADR and docs/BDR under docs/decision-records - 78 files, 53 links broken - with no question asked. The repository's convention lost to the standard's by default.

points.asks: Does this repository run at the `core` profile or the `scale` one - is the work handed off between people, or does one person carry each piece end to end?
points.why: green.stack asks this on the greenfield path, bundled with the stack, and nothing asks it on the brownfield one - where the manifest is copied in early and carries a default profile. A repository that adopts under the wrong profile is scored against gates its team does not run, or silently excused from ones it does. There is no convergent answer here: `scale` is not a fuller adoption than `core` (ADR-011), it is a different shape, and pushing a solo repo onto the team gate is how a standard gets reverted. Ask it by hand-off, never by headcount or sprints: the first repository asked chose neither option and typed its own - several people, no sprints, tasks taken off a backlog - which is `scale` by the only axis that matters and reads as `core` by both of the ones that do not.

points.asks: How far does this adoption go: migrate everything to the standard, adopt selected parts, or assess only and change nothing yet?
points.why: Everything downstream is scoped by this answer, so inferring it means inferring the whole run.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: docs/adoption-intake.md quotes the owner declaring full migration in a sentence he never typed. The transcript holds one user turn and it does not say that.

points.asks: This session can be kept as evidence for the standard - the questions it asked, the answers you gave, what it produced. Send an anonymised excerpt upstream as a pull request, after you have read it?
points.why: Asked at the close, it is never asked at all: the run has just produced its artifacts, the user is waiting for a pull request, and the last steps of a long phase file are the ones a run does not reach. Asked in the intake round, it fires where every other adoption question already fires. It asks one thing and leads with sending because the first shape led with keeping and closed with recording nothing: the safe-looking answer was the one that sent nothing, and it was the one taken. No option is recommended (ADR-055). The adoption ping is not one of its answers - it carries no session content and goes out on its own (ADR-047).
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: a full adoption - 25 commits, 253 files, 20 questions asked - reached none of its three closing steps. No transcript was offered, and the adoption counter the standard publishes stayed at 12 while the run finished. 2026-09-03: with the list led by keep-it-local and closed by do-not-keep, adopters took the last answer, so nothing reached upstream from adoptions that completed.

points.asks: Phase finished. Continue to the next one, stop here, or hand the rest back to you?
points.gates: starting any phase after the first
points.why: A guided adoption that runs to the end unprompted and stops at a summary is not guided. The checkpoint is also where the human can redirect before the next phase writes anything.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: the run ended on a summary; the owner had to prompt it himself to carry on.

points.asks: This repository holds informal working material - scratch notes, PRDs, plans, TODO files - that the standard has a home for. Route it into discovery and the backlog now, list it for you to triage, or leave it untouched?
points.gates: any edit to informal material, and the discovery record
points.why: Unfinished work written down informally is the highest-value thing an adoption can find, because it is knowledge the repository already paid for and nothing indexes. Editing those files without reading them for content is the worst of both: the notes are disturbed and their contents are still lost.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: .scratch holds 21 directories and 56 markdown files - 5 PRDs, 5 plans, 5 specs, 2 task lists, a test-gaps note. The adoption opened them only to rewrite links, and separately deferred docs/TODO triage on its own authority.

points.asks: This repository already has decision records, and the standard expects more. Take what is there as it stands, rewrite it into the standard's shape, or leave it and only add new ones? And for the new ones - write them now, leave stubs, or have them drafted for you to check later?
points.recommended: rewrite them into the standard's shape
points.gates: docs/decision-records/** - a new record, and an edit to one that was already there
points.why: A decision record is the one artifact whose whole value is that a person decided it.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: 33 owner-authored records each gained a '## Revisit when' section nobody asked for.

points.asks: Who are the users of this product? Define them yourself, have them suggested from the code for you to correct, or skip personas for now?
points.why: Personas are a claim about people outside the repository. Nothing in the code can settle them.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: five personas invented, roster declared closed, no inferred marker despite onboard.md requiring one.

points.asks: The standard's backlog.md is the source of truth for tracked work, and this repository already tracks work elsewhere. Fold that into the backlog, keep both with the backlog as the source, or keep the external tracker and let the backlog bridge to it?
points.gates: backlog.md - the first row written into it
points.why: Two live trackers is the state a repository drifts into by inertia, and it is worse than either one alone: both stay, both rot differently, and which one is true gets decided per person.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: the agent asked this question without it being declared anywhere, and recommended keeping the repository's own tracker beside backlog.md - the least convergent answer on offer.

points.asks: Should the adoption seed a backlog, and if so how is the work attributed - each row naming the role it needs, assigned to you by name, or with nothing said about who does it?
points.recommended: seed it, each row naming the role it needs
points.why: Assigning work to a named person is an act with consequences outside the repository, and in a one- or two-person repo the name is the same on every row, which makes it noise. The role is the part that is always true: it says what kind of work the row is without claiming anybody agreed to it.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: 20 items written with owners and definitions of done, unasked.

points.asks: The repository already has agent guards that overlap the standard's. Replace, merge, or keep both?
points.gates: hooks and guard configuration in the target repository
points.why: Overwriting a working guard can silently remove protection, and a silent guard is indistinguishable from a healthy one.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: the single question the whole run did ask. It was asked because the duplication was mechanically visible - which is precisely why the other points, being invisible, were never raised.

points.asks: This adoption touches many files. Split the work into commits how - one per concern, one per phase, or a single change?
points.gates: the first commit of the adoption branch
points.why: Under rebase merge every commit lands in main on its own, so granularity is the reviewer's contract, not a formatting preference.
points.evidence: stayget 2026-08-19: three commits for roughly 200 changed files, chosen by the agent.

points.asks: What is this going to be, and who is it for?
points.why: An empty repository contains no evidence, so anything the agent writes here is invention by construction.

points.asks: Do you have naming and structure conventions you want carried in, or should the standard's defaults apply?
points.why: Same defect as adopt.layout, one step earlier: the cheapest moment to honour someone's convention is before any file exists. It is asked on both paths and it was declared on only one: the first field run reached it on the brownfield path, where no file asked it, invented the question and recommended that the repository's own conventions win - the same cautious drift the declaration exists to stop, on the one path nothing checked.

points.asks: Which stack, and which profile - core or scale?
What is in scope for this specification, and what is explicitly out?
points.why: The skill's own description promises 'Asks one question at a time' and has no mechanism to ask anything.

points.asks: What must be true for this to count as done?
points.why: Acceptance criteria written by the party that will satisfy them are not criteria.

points.asks: These points are undetermined. Decide them now, mark them provisional, or leave them open?
points.why: Silently resolving an unknown is the failure mode; naming it as unresolved is the whole job.

points.asks: What existing material should this draw on, and where does it live?
points.why: Discovery already carries the idea of provenance for materials; it just never asks whose they are.

points.asks: Which of the decisions surfaced here are already settled, and which are still open?
points.gates: any decision record produced by discovery
points.why: A settled decision and an assumed one are indistinguishable once written down.

points.asks: Whose run is this - yours, or someone else's - and may the transcript excerpt be kept as evidence?
points.why: The skill that records human participation was itself the one that recorded a person who does not exist.
points.evidence: The corpus entry framed as an external adopter, with an anonymity caveat nobody requested, was the repository author's own run. External adopters: zero.

$gate_globs: Paths a write must not reach before the point is answered. Only points whose artifact is a file appear here. adopt.layout gates a rename, which the hook does see; the rest gate something it cannot - a phase boundary, a commit, guard configuration whose path the repository chooses, a layout that does not exist yet, a decision inside a spec - and the static check and human review carry those. Saying that here beats leaving a reader to assume full coverage.
$recommended_answer: Every point declares which answer is recommended, and the skill offers it first. Two axes decide it and both point the same way: the answer that converges on the standard - its layout, its shape, the whole of it - and the answer a person gives now rather than defers. Keeping the repository's own way stays on the list, because a standard imposed without consent gets reverted; it is never the default. Left to choose, an agent recommends the cautious option and adoption becomes an opt-in menu - measured on stayget 2026-08-19, where four of five recommendations pointed at the least convergent answer, including 'keep yours and map' for the layout. null means the point has no such axis: record.participation asks for consent, and consent is never nudged. A point asked on more than one path lists every file that asks it, because the copy nobody checked is the one that drifts: the first field run reached green.conventions on the brownfield path, where no file declared it, and recommended that the repository's own conventions win. elicitation-points-check reads this against the option order of every call site, so the two cannot drift apart - it can check the text where it is written, never the question as spoken, because a question asked in the user's own language does not match any string we could hold here.
$scope: Whether the answer belongs to the repository or to the piece of work in front of you, and it decides what satisfies the hook. A `repository` point is asked once - who the product is for, what the layout is, which profile it runs at - so once the ledger carries an answered row and that row is committed, later sessions write the artifact without asking again. A `work` point is asked every time, because the answer belongs to this spec, this digest, this run: no committed row can stand in for the scope of a specification nobody has written yet. Getting this wrong in either direction breaks the layer - treat every point as `work` and an ordinary `adr-write` in an adopted repo is refused until it re-asks an adoption question, which ends with the guard deleted; treat every point as `repository` and one answer at adoption time licenses every write for the life of the repo.
